Much more of a philosophy course than a science course which can be misleading, and many figures mentioned in class hold prejudiced views when looked up. professor hoffman is super nice and her lectures are very clear (she spends a lot of time explaining in different ways so that it sticks), the class structure and teaching style reminds me of 14a with professor creel. attendance in lectures and discussion arent mandatory and all lectures are recorded

analysis.name: Andrew Huberman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's like the Justin Timberlake of neuroscience; legit though. He is really knowledgeable, down to earth, lectures are attention holding, really good class. No textbook, readings consist of modern research papers. Recommend.

Dr. Huberman is a great lecturer. The material can be intimidating (seems to be taught at a graduate level) but his main goal is to invoke scientific curiosity and teach students how to analyze and understand scientific papers. He assigns papers each week for a group to analyze and present during section. Very good practice for the MT and final.

Dr. Huberman is one of the few exceptional teachers that truly cares about his students' learning. He won't force you to memorize asinine facts -- instead he'll give you the tools to learn neuroscience from research, like an actual neuroscientist does.  He is a gifted, captivating lecturer and great at explaining complex material. Highly recommend!
One of the most student-centric professors at UCSD. Easy class, interesting, you learn some cool material,  overall very enjoyable academic class.   Take him if you can.

He's an entertaining and knowledgeable lecturer if you choose to go to lecture. One group project, a midterm, and a final. Discussion is mandatory but you just go over papers, which you should read because they help you prepare for the exams. Learn the different methods used and you'll do well. Easy A class as long as you do a little work!

Professor Medvetz is an amazing lecturer! Be prepared to talk a lot and engage in conversations in class. His lectures were interesting and he tried to connect the theories we learned to current problems and/or movies, which made all the information we learned easier to digest. 2 writing assignments (a 4-page and an 8-page), final exam, and discussions were mandatory.

The amount of effort he put in to help us understand the material is unreal to me. I'm on exchange and none of my professors at my home university would ever go to the lengths he went to if they miss class. Medvetz was down with the flu for a week and delivered 2 video lectures that he sent to us so that we didn't have to rush through it.

Professor Zroka's lectures felt very inhuman. She was basically reading off a script and her voice made it seem like she was screaming at us the whole time. But, as a hum, your grade really depends on your ta.
She was nice and as long as you try and do your work she give you fulll points on assignments. no the best writer but I got an A in class and passed my portfolio.

Prof Zroka helped me with revising my essays, I would say go to office hours once you start writing them instead of going until the end of the quarter as that's when everyone decides to go. I went early and her feedback helped me and she made time to clarify any questions that I had. Overall a good professor but class can get boring.

Professor Zroka is an alright professor. Her lectures are direct and straightforward but are pretty boring. Helped me touch up on writing in this class. Her feedback is straightforward but isn't very detailed.

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are just him restating what is in the book. Honestly I learn more from the book that I do from his lectures. He has quizzes every week and they are unreasonably difficult. I understand the 142 series is hard but the quizzes are so confusing and he doesn't give us enough examples that would help. No piazza either. Youre on your own here

Instead of watching the lectures you should just read the textbook since they're exactly the same. His quizzes are relatively straightforward. The true/false portion of the quizzes is worth too much in my opinion (4/10 points of quiz) and there are only 2 true falses so if you miss one you're already at a 8/10. Overall the class is structured well.

Zucker will teach you just fine but not exceptionally well. The textbook and your own notes/understanding are your best bet at passing. Towards the end I stopped attending class and just read the book. The curve for this class is very, very generous as it was for the last class he taught so if you take Zucker you can probably expect to be curved.

This course is the 1st that he taught in person at UCSD, and I can positively say that his lecturing style is superb in person, but would suck through Zoom, which explains a lot of the bad ratings. Spend some time going over the lecture notes yourself, since the course material can be abstract and can't be absorbed right away during lecture.

Pretty easy homework but I barely went to lecture so I just taught myself since his lectures are just straight out of the book, like word for word.
